items.title: No Surprises Act nonpayment cases flood courts to little effect - Modern Healthcare
items.reason: This article directly addresses No Surprises Act litigation and enforcement outcomes, which is a core component of the topic definition covering federal litigation related to NSA enforcement.
items.summary: Courts are experiencing a surge in No Surprises Act nonpayment cases, but these lawsuits are producing limited practical results in enforcing the law's protections. The article examines the litigation landscape emerging from NSA enforcement efforts, indicating that despite increased court filings related to nonpayment disputes under the Act, the outcomes are not effectively advancing compliance or balance-billing protections. This development matters for revenue-cycle teams as it suggests the litigation pathway may have limited utility for recovering disputed claims or enforcing NSA requirements, potentially shifting focus toward other enforcement mechanisms like the IDR process or regulatory remedies.

items.title: No Surprises Act Arbitration May Narrow Networks and Raise ACA Marketplace Premiums - Substack
items.reason: The item directly addresses No Surprises Act implementation and its effects on networks and premiums through the arbitration/IDR process, which is within the scope of NSA rulemaking and enforcement impacts, though a Substack analysis may present interpretive rather than news-driven content.
items.summary: A Substack analysis examines how the No Surprises Act's arbitration mechanisms (specifically the Independent Dispute Resolution process) may unintentionally narrow insurance networks and increase ACA marketplace premiums. The author argues that the IDR process for resolving out-of-network payment disputes could incentivize insurers to restrict provider networks to avoid arbitration costs, ultimately affecting plan affordability and network access. This development matters for revenue-cycle teams because it directly impacts how out-of-network payment disputes are resolved and may influence provider contracting strategies and reimbursement rates.

items.title: Elevance Health rolls out new site-of-care billing policies
items.reason: Elevance Health's new site-of-care billing policies directly align with the topic's focus on payer policies affecting provider reimbursement and network status, similar to the Anthem/Elevance out-of-network facility penalty examples in the rubric.
items.summary: Elevance Health (formerly Anthem) has announced new site-of-care billing policies designed to ensure services are reimbursed at appropriate payment levels and increase transparency regarding where patients receive care. These policies represent a shift in how the major payer determines reimbursement based on care setting, which can significantly impact provider revenue depending on whether services are delivered in hospital, ambulatory surgery center, or office settings. Revenue-cycle teams must monitor the specific payment rules, effective dates, and any geographic variations in implementation to accurately forecast reimbursement changes and adjust billing and negotiation strategies accordingly.

items.title: Attorney General Ellison seeks community input on proposed acquisition of Essentia Health by HealthPartners - Minnesota Attorney General's Office
items.reason: This involves a state attorney general's review of a health insurer/payer acquisition (HealthPartners acquiring Essentia Health), which falls within payer regulatory enforcement and oversight activities that can affect revenue-cycle operations through network changes and payer policy modifications.
items.summary: Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison is soliciting community input on HealthPartners' proposed acquisition of Essentia Health, signaling regulatory review of the transaction. The acquisition would affect a significant regional health system and payer entity, potentially influencing provider networks, claims-processing relationships, and contracting terms for healthcare providers. State attorney general scrutiny of payer acquisitions can result in conditions, restrictions, or enforcement actions that impact how providers interact with and receive payment from the combined entity. Revenue-cycle teams should monitor this review for potential changes to network status, credentialing processes, and payment terms once the acquisition is approved or conditional approval is issued.
